label: Mid-input token (t=3-7) in sequences starting with f/c/d/3/x/r/o, gated by current token identity
explanation: Fires almost only during the original input phase at steps 3-7 (96% of mass; peaks at t=4), with a small leak onto the <DEL> step and never in the copy phase or at t<2. It looks like the sum of two factors. (1) The first original token: rate is 2.3-3.4x when it is f, c, d, 3, x, r or o, and 1.4x for l. (2) The current input token: b and j are strongest (3x), then m, g, z, 0, u, 2, i, 1. It prefers first occurrences of a token (in_first gives 89% of mass). The conjunction of the first-token set and the strong current-token set is 93% precise but recalls only 33%. The broader recorded predicate gets dev P=0.81, R=0.48, mass recall 0.67. Top activations combine both factors, e.g. f d 1 [b] [b] [g]. The misses are weaker activations that have only one of the two factors, so this is a graded additive code and not a clean binary feature. It does not fire on copy-phase outputs.
